beats.beat: A B Infrabuild operates in two segments: infrastructure creation (railways, bridges, roads) and operating a Ready Mix Concrete plant at Kashimira, Thane.

Contracts are won through a competitive tender process: the client floats a tender, the company bids, and the lowest quote typically wins. A performance guarantee must be deposited before work begins.
Major clients include Municipal Corporation of Greater Mumbai, Western Railway, Central Railway, Mumbai Railway Vikas Corporation Ltd, MMRDA, and Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation of India Ltd.
Western Railway alone contributed 52% of the orders on hand as of the filing date.
The company uses the 'Box Pushing' technique for construction, which it considers a modern innovation.
Its competitive strengths are listed as quality, transparency, long-standing client relationships, experienced management, a healthy order book, and state-of-the-art machinery.

beats.beat: Revenue from operations has declined from ₹9,021.12 lakhs in FY2015 to ₹6,053.05 lakhs in FY2018, a drop of about 33% over three years.
Net profit after adjustments was erratic: ₹95.95 lakhs in FY2014, ₹78.36 lakhs in FY2015, ₹32.63 lakhs in FY2016, a sharp drop to ₹15.86 lakhs in FY2017, then a surge to ₹314.66 lakhs in FY2018.
Profit before interest, depreciation and tax (EBITDA) stood at ₹928.80 lakhs in FY2018, up from ₹676.19 lakhs in FY2017 and ₹783.31 lakhs in FY2016.
Short-term borrowings increased from ₹3,082.27 lakhs in FY2014 to ₹3,537.35 lakhs in FY2018, while long-term borrowings fell sharply from ₹672.72 lakhs to ₹133.09 lakhs over the same period.
The company has reported negative cash flows in recent years, a risk it acknowledges.
Total assets grew from ₹7,062.34 lakhs in FY2014 to ₹8,232.15 lakhs in FY2018, driven by current assets.

beats.beat: The promoter, Amit Bholanath Mishra, holds 74,95,476 equity shares, representing 90.949% of the pre-issue capital.
Key management personnel include Ms. Anchal Pachori (CFO, aged 28, CA) and Mr. Mohit Soni (Company Secretary, aged 26, ACS).

Related-party transactions in FY2018 included loans taken from KMP/Directors of ₹68.4 lakhs and director remuneration of ₹57.7 lakhs; outstanding payables to related parties were ₹324.3 lakhs as of March 31, 2018.
Two companies promoted by the promoter — Al-Noor Chickens Private Limited and A B Magma Automobiles Private Limited — were struck off by the Registrar of Companies in March 2016 due to non-operation.
The company has issued equity shares in the past 12 months at a price that may be lower than the issue price, a potential concern for pricing.
No independent monitoring agency has been appointed to oversee the use of issue proceeds.

beats.beat: The infrastructure sector includes power, bridges, dams, roads and urban infrastructure, contributing about 8% to India's GDP at constant prices.
The construction market was valued at US$400 billion in 2015 and is projected to reach US$1 trillion by 2025.
Growth drivers include government flagship programs (100 Smart Cities, AMRUT, Make in India), eased FDI norms in 15 sectors, and rising urbanization and disposable income.
India's GDP growth was above 7% in 2017, and the logistics sector is expected to grow at a CAGR of 10.5% to US$215 billion by 2020.
However, the industry is highly fragmented, working capital intensive, and subject to slow pace of government projects and changes in government policies.
Competition comes from both organized and unorganized players.

beats.beat: A B Infrabuild Limited is an infrastructure construction company based in Mumbai, Maharashtra, that builds railway platforms, bridges, roads and operates a Ready Mix Concrete plant.
It has been a vendor to Western Railway since 2006 and counts government bodies like MCGM, MMRDA and Central Railway among its clients.
The company is now seeking to raise capital through an initial public offering of 44,28,000 equity shares on the SME platform of a stock exchange.
Its promoter, Amit Bholanath Mishra, owns 90.9% of the company and has been in the industry for over 20 years.

intro.purpose: Orient the reader: who the company is, what it does, what it is raising, and why it matters.

beats.beat: The issue comprises 44,28,000 equity shares of ₹10 each, all fresh issue (no offer for sale). The issue price will be determined through book building.
The lead manager to the issue is Mark Corporate Advisors Private Limited.
The registrar is Bigshare Services Private Limited.
Proceeds are allocated primarily to meet working capital requirements (₹1,130 lakhs) and the balance for general corporate purposes; the exact allocation for corporate purposes is not disclosed.
No independent appraisal agency has been appointed for the project, and no monitoring agency has been appointed — fund deployment is at the discretion of the management and board.

beats.beat: Client concentration: Western Railway accounted for 52% of the order book and Indian Railways as a whole contributed 57% of revenue in FY2018. Loss of this customer would severely impact revenue.
Negative cash flows: The company has experienced negative cash flows in recent years, which could impair its ability to fund working capital and service debt.
Order book cancellations: Contracts in the order book may be adjusted, cancelled or suspended by clients, and the order book is not a guarantee of future revenue.
High short-term debt: Short-term borrowings stood at ₹3,537.35 lakhs as of March 2018, exceeding the company's net worth and exposing it to refinancing risk and high interest costs.

Related-party transactions and promoter-linked companies: The promoter has had two companies struck off, and the company has significant outstanding payables to related parties, raising governance concerns.
